title: Separate scale offsets widen the allowed inclination range of 18 APOGEE CPV hosts
abstract: We test the spin inclination inference for complex periodic variable (CPV) hosts. Fresh TIC v8.2 and APOGEE DR17 queries recover 18 hosts and 119 controls. Hosts have a narrow distribution of projected velocity times period divided by radius, but its median exceeds the physical sin i limit. With isotropic controls, separate host and control scales lower AIC by about 24 relative to a common scale. The nominal upper cutoff in host cos i grows from 0.34 to 0.90. The separate-scale model still favors an inclination cutoff over full isotropy, with twice the log likelihood gain 7.13. A scale-free simulation reproduces the published narrow-width probability of 0.0115. If selection excludes the lowest-inclination tenth of an isotropic population, that probability rises to 0.0731. For eight TESS hosts alone it rises from 0.0681 to 0.1531. This is a sensitivity test, not a measurement of the selection function or a rejection of equatorial clouds. Small samples, uncertain line broadening, radii, control orientations and random-error assumptions limit the result. Code, aggregate evidence, input hashes and separate-scratch retrieval steps are included.

display.caption: Left: the host-width simulation becomes less restrictive when selection removes a small low-inclination tail. Right: separate-scale likelihood profiles allow broad angular ranges. Neither test measures the actual selection function.

citations.reason: Reuses MIT retrieval code and repeats the inclination sample. Tests how scale and selection assumptions change the near-edge-on inference. Does not challenge its H-alpha or X-ray measurements.
